newsitem.title: FRANCE: French chef Constant to make new start.
newsitem.headline: French chef Constant to make new start.

text.p: Chef Christian Constant put the final touch to an eventful year for French cuisine by announcing on Monday he would leave the famed kitchen of the Paris Hotel Crillon to open his own restaurant.

In a newspaper interview, the 46-year-old Constant said he was tired of working up to 14 hours a day and was looking forward to a new start in his restaurant, opening next month in the capital's chic seventh district across the river Seine.
Constant hinted that he made his decision after the Crillon's restaurant, on Concorde square, failed once again to win the coveted three-star rating in the latest Michelin guide.
"I think we were regularly at the level (of a three-star restaurant) and with my team, we did the maximum to earn it," he told the daily Le Figaro.
Constant's decision came five months after Joel Robuchon, regarded by many as France's greatest chef, cooked his last meal at the legendary three-star Paris restaurant that bore his name.
Alain Ducasse, who made his reputation at the Louis XV in Monaco, opted to take over from Robuchon.
1996 also brought a statement by a dozen celebrity chefs saying foreign flavours were polluting the purity of French cuisine.

Constant told Le Figaro that sophisticated cooking was no longer fashionable and promised to return to basics in his new restaurant, which would serve such traditional dishes as cassoulet or lamb navarin.
"A good restaurant today must be simple, good and accessible," he said.
